title: Go SDK: stream watchdog protocol and cooperative abort examples
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Streaming RPCs in the Go SDK currently rely on context cancellation and timeouts alone to trigger stream termination. In production we see two problem classes: (1) client stalls where the caller loses interest but doesn't cancel (leaking server resources and KV cache entries), and (2) partial writes or network partitions where neither side clearly terminates and retries lead to duplicate logical requests.

Goal: Implement a lightweight per-stream watchdog (heartbeat) + cooperative abort protocol in the Go SDK runtime to ensure predictable cleanup and safe retry semantics, with examples and tests. Deliver end-to-end guidance for application authors on when to use context cancellation vs. the new watchdog.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design and ship a Go SDK helper that manages a per-stream watchdog timer and optional heartbeat message semantics for long-running streams.
- Provide a cooperative abort handshake (client signals intent to abort; server responds ack and then drains) integrated in the existing stream frame protocol.
- Add documented examples demonstrating: graceful client-initiated abort, server-initiated abort on idle/heartbeat failure, and how to combine context timeouts with watchdogs for lenient vs strict termination policies.
- Instrumentation hooks for Console traces: emitted events for watchdog-fired, abort-requested, abort-acknowledged, and final-closed.
- Unit + integration tests that simulate partial network loss and verify at-most-once semantics for idempotent operations.

Non-goals: changing server-side long-lived session design beyond the cooperative abort frames, implementing binary protocol changes outside the SDK helper, or altering billing semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New Go helper API shipped: StreamWatchdog{Start(ctx), Kick(), RequestAbort(), WaitClosed(ctx)} with clear doc comments.
2) Examples added to repo under examples/stream-watchdog demonstrating code patterns and backoff/retry guidance.
3) Four new trace events emitted and visible in Console when feature flag enabled.
4) Integration test simulating stalled client that did not cancel its ctx; server frees KV cache and stream entries within configured grace period.
5) Backwards compatible: unchanged behavior when helper is not used (defaults off).
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket creation. Observed leaks in customer sandbox where client-side goroutine stuck waiting on read; they never cancelled. Proposed watchdog to enforce cleanup after 30s grace by default.

2026-02-28 - Diego Morales: Reviewed design draft. Decided to implement helper at SDK layer rather than runtime core to keep server compatibility. Will add events consumable by Console traces. Assigned to myself for initial prototype.

2026-03-03 - Diego Morales: Prototype completed. API shape: StreamWatchdog(ctx, opts...) returns a controller. Implementation uses time.Timer + Kick() called on every successful receive/send. Added RequestAbort() which sends a control frame; server must respond with AbortAck frame. If server doesn't ack before grace period, watchdog forces close and records event.

2026-03-05 - Design review - Jenna Park: UX feedback: Make RequestAbort non-blocking with an opt-in blocking WaitClosed(ctx) for callers who need to ensure drain completed. Also add example showing combining context.WithTimeout + watchdog.Kick() for streaming generation where token production may pause.

2026-03-07 - Diego Morales: Added integration test harness that injects a one-way partition (client->server) to validate server abort path. Found a race where streaming goroutine and watchdog attempted to close transport concurrently; fixed by routing all closes through single closeOnce wrapper in sdk/stream/transport.go.

2026-03-09 - QA - Ravi Patel: Ran flaky test suite 10x against prototype; two failures observed related to telemetry emission ordering. Added a buffered events queue to reduce contention and ensure stable ordering for traces. QA +1 after two more runs.

2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Preparing PR. Items remaining: doc examples in examples/stream-watchdog, Console schema review (events names), and update to CHANGELOG under sdk-go-0.18.0. Planning to open PR today: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/1782
notes:
Design trade-offs considered:
- Option A: push watchdog into runtime to allow server-initiated enforcement. Rejected for risk and compatibility.
- Option B: SDK helper that uses control frames for cooperative abort; server support optional and will fall back to forced-close semantics. Chosen for incremental roll-out.
- Option C: rely solely on context deadlines. Insufficient for clients that stop calling but don't cancel (common in serverless misuse patterns).

Telemetry events: [stream.watchdog.fired, stream.abort.requested, stream.abort.ack, stream.closed.final] - include stream_id, session_id, triggered_by (watchdog|caller|server), elapsed_ms. Console team requested event schema review (ticket PM-411).
Suggested defaults: grace_period=30s, heartbeat_interval=10s, max_unacked_heartbeats=3. Expose via opts and environment variable for ops teams.

Security notes: the control frame is informational (cooperative). No sensitive payloads. Still flagged for review if we add control payloads in future (security_review_required = false for this phase).
